title: Africa capitals four of six · The Horn and the Great Lakes
edition: Africa capitals · Six regional lessons · John · November 2026
intro: Welcome to the Africa capitals, episode four of six. First, I clear the chosen names for a fresh regional lesson.
We turn to the Horn of Africa at the Red Sea, then inland to the great lakes of the equator.

states.name: Djibouti
lines: Djibouti stands at the head of the Gulf of Tadjoura, on the Bab-el-Mandeb strait, in the small country the map names Djibouti.
A railway runs from the Ethiopian highlands down to this harbour, and the Lake Assal depression below sea level, with its salt crust, lies close by.
Remember the harbour at the strait, where the rail line from inland Ethiopia comes down to the sea.

states.name: Asmara
lines: Asmara stands in the Eritrean highlands, well inland from the long Red Sea coast below it.
The capital preserves an exceptional group of early modernist buildings from Italian colonial rule, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2017.
Remember the modernist highland capital, high above Eritrea’s Red Sea coast.

states.name: Addis Ababa
lines: Addis Ababa stands on the Ethiopian highland plateau, west of the Horn of Africa and south of Eritrea.
The national museum keeps the Middle Awash fossils, including the famous “Lucy” specimen, and the city’s name means “new flower”.
Remember the new flower at 2,355 metres, the highland capital whose national museum holds Lucy.
states.transition: Let's bring Addis Ababa into view.

states.name: Mogadishu
lines: Mogadishu stands on the Indian Ocean, in the south of Somalia, at the bottom of the Horn.
One of the oldest trading cities of East Africa, Ibn Battuta found it rich when he visited in 1331, and its Arba’a Rukun mosque dates from 1269.
Remember the Indian Ocean harbour at the foot of the Horn, where a traveller found a rich trading city in 1331.

states.name: Hargeisa
lines: Hargeisa is the capital of Somaliland, a self-declared state that the United Nations treats as part of Somalia; Somalia’s own capital is Mogadishu.
It was largely destroyed in the war of 1988 and rebuilt as the seat of Somaliland’s government; its camel market is now one of the largest in the Horn of Africa.
Remember the two Somali capitals: Hargeisa in the northern interior, Mogadishu on the Indian Ocean in the south.

states.name: Kampala
lines: Kampala stands on the hills above Lake Victoria in Uganda, west of Kenya.
The Kasubi Tombs on one of those hills hold the burial places of the Kabaka kings, and were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2001.
Remember the royal tombs on the hills above Lake Victoria.

states.name: Nairobi
lines: Nairobi stands in Kenya, inland from the Indian Ocean, on the high ground above the Rift Valley lakes.

It began in 1899 as a depot on the railway from Mombasa to Uganda, and today a national park with lions and giraffes lies in sight of its tower blocks; its name is often read from a Maasai phrase for “cool water”.
Remember the “cool water” capital: the railway depot that grew up between a national park and the highlands.

states.name: Kigali
lines: Kigali stands in the hills of Rwanda, north of Burundi and west of Tanzania.
The memorial at Gisozi keeps the memory of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi, and the capital has since become one of the greenest cities in Africa.
Remember the green hills of Rwanda, and the memorial standing above the capital.

states.name: Gitega
lines: Gitega stands in the centre of Burundi, inland from the Lake Tanganyika shore, in the middle of the country.
It is the old royal town, and it replaced Bujumbura as the capital in 2019; the royal drum sanctuary of Gishora is close by.
Remember the inland centre that took over from the lakeside capital, with Rwanda just to the north.

states.name: Dodoma
lines: Dodoma stands inland in central Tanzania, south of Kenya and west of the Indian Ocean coast.
It was chosen as the capital in 1973, near the middle of the country so that the seat of government would be close to every region, and the State House stands on a hill above the town.
Remember the inland capital chosen in the middle of Tanzania, below Kenya and far from the sea.

recap: Djibouti guards the strait where the railway from inland Ethiopia reaches the sea, Asmara keeps its modernist highland buildings, Addis Ababa holds Lucy’s country, and Mogadishu faces the Indian Ocean.

Remember the two Somali capitals, Hargeisa inland in the north and Mogadishu on the ocean in the south, then the royal tombs above Lake Victoria at Kampala, the railway capital and its park at Nairobi, the green hills at Kigali, the inland centre at Gitega and the middle-of-Tanzania capital at Dodoma.
